primary_claim: The top right singular vectors of the layer-to-layer Jacobian ('Power Steering'), computable in ~15 forward passes via power iteration, produce steering vectors comparable in performance to costlier nonlinear MELBO optimization, both amplifying decision-fork behaviours (e.g. anti-refusal, corrigibility) and eliciting latent behaviours (e.g. boosting arithmetic accuracy on Qwen3-1.7B-Base from 6% to 90% via chain-of-thought elicitation).

effect.metric: arithmetic accuracy after steering vs. baseline; steering effectiveness vs. MELBO/CAA
effect.value: best power-steering vector boosted Qwen3-1.7B-Base arithmetic accuracy from 6% to 90%; power steering achieved comparable corrigibility-steering performance to MELBO, both outperforming CAA on steerability, at ~15 forward passes per layer pair

stated_future_work: Extend the full sensitivity-map approach to Qwen3-14B to find better source/target layer pairs for corrigibility steering, rather than heuristic-chosen ones
Evaluate scale selection more rigorously than the current fixed norm-based scaling
Develop a better selection criterion than KL divergence for identifying useful steering vectors
Add padding vectors / increase oversampling to improve accuracy of higher-ranked singular vectors in the near-degenerate spectrum
limitations_stated: Power iteration is noisy in the near-degenerate singular-value subspace past the top ~5 vectors
Power iteration recovers vectors only up to sign; only one sign was evaluated per vector, so behaviourally significant directions may have been missed
KL divergence is a noisy proxy for behavioural change and not a guarantee of an interesting effect
The method finds directions the network is already sensitive to, so it may be fundamentally limited to amplifying latent behaviours rather than inducing genuinely new ones
The corrigibility datasets likely have some contamination effect since Qwen3-8B was probably trained on them
quote: The best vector found (source 7 to target 25, right singular vector 1) boosted accuracy from 6% to 90%.
